items.text: NDA (after 12th) and TES (10+2, JEE-based) are the earliest officer-entry doors; CDS is the main route after a bachelor's degree.

blocks.heading: Use the Four Questions Before You Commit

items.text: A pay table or a pension rule cannot tell you whether a defence career actually fits your temperament and your family's situation.

A defence career rewards people who can sit with discipline, hierarchy, and physical demand for years without treating it as a temporary phase, and who genuinely want to lead or serve alongside people under real pressure, not just wear the uniform in family photos.

If the idea of daily physical training, drill, and strict hierarchy for years genuinely drains you rather than steadies you, that is a real signal worth taking seriously before you commit a training slot.
A defence services career India delivers real stability, respect, and structure, but it also asks for things most desk-job career comparisons never mention.
Officers and other ranks get posted where the service needs them, field areas, high-altitude posts, remote border locations, and peace stations in rotation, typically every 2-3 years.

Medical standards for defence entries are strict and specific (eyesight, BMI, dental, and more), and a disqualification at the SSB medical stage after months of preparation is a genuinely common outcome.

blocks.heading: Waste an Attempt or Years of Service

items.text: NDA and TES training itself weeds out people who cannot sustain years of drill, physical training, and hierarchy, test your own tolerance honestly before you commit at 17.
Only Permanent Commission officers, and SSC officers who cross the relevant service threshold or are later granted PC, draw a service pension.
Decide, with your family, whether you can genuinely sustain transfers every 2-3 years, extended separations, and remote postings before you sign up, not after your first posting order arrives.

visuals.heading: NDA After 12th

figures.label: Estimated Time Required
figures.source: NDA (National Defence Academy) is open to Class 12 pass candidates roughly 16.5 to 19.5 years old. The Army wing accepts any stream; Navy and Air Force wings require Physics and Mathematics at 12th level. Selection runs through a UPSC written exam (Mathematics and General Ability), held twice a year, followed by the SSB interview and a medical exam.
figures.text: The Army wing accepts any stream; Navy and Air Force wings require Physics and Mathematics at 12th level. Selection runs through a UPSC written exam (Mathematics and General Ability), held twice a year, followed by the SSB interview and a medical exam.

figures.label: Total Course Duration
figures.source: Selected cadets train for 3 years at NDA Khadakwasla across all three services together, then move to their respective service academy for 1 more year of specialised training before commissioning as an officer. That is a 4-year commitment before you even draw a full officer's salary, the longest runway of any entry route on this list, and the one that locks in the earliest.

figures.label: Estimated Time Required
figures.source: Since 2022, most fresh recruitment into other-ranks positions across the Army, Navy, and Air Force runs through the Agnipath scheme. Eligible candidates are roughly 17.5 to 21 years old for the Navy and 17.5 to 23 for the Army and Air Force, with a 10th or 12th pass requirement depending on the trade applied for.
figures.text: Since 2022, most fresh recruitment into other-ranks positions across the Army, Navy, and Air Force runs through the Agnipath scheme.

figures.label: Typical Salary Range
figures.source: Selected Agniveers serve a fixed 4-year tenure, receiving full training, salary, and allowances during that period. At the end of the tenure, up to 25% of each batch is retained for full regular service - continuing under the standard other-ranks pay and pension structure, while the remaining 75% exit with a tax-free Seva Nidhi package (commonly reported around Rs 11.71 lakh) and a service-specific skill certificate.

figures.label: Estimated Time Required
figures.source: Agnipath is genuinely the lowest-commitment way to test whether military life fits you, since the tenure is fixed at 4 years rather than an open-ended career. Treat those 4 years as an active test-and-plan window, not a guaranteed on-ramp to permanent service, plan a second-career track alongside it, not only after your exit date is confirmed.

blocks.heading: Commissioned Officer Starts As a Lieutenant

figures.label: Estimated Time Required
figures.source: Colonel rank (roughly 16 years of service, Pay Level 13) and Brigadier rank (Pay Level 13A) are selection-based, not time-based, and a meaningful share of officers who reach Lieutenant Colonel do not go further, simply because there are far fewer Colonel and Brigadier posts than Lieutenant Colonels competing for them.

figures.label: Pension Eligibility Period
figures.source: Permanent Commission officers and other ranks who complete the pensionable qualifying period (broadly 20 years for officers, shorter for some other-ranks categories) draw a pension based on rank and last pay drawn. Short Service Commission officers who leave before 10-14 years and are not granted Permanent Commission generally do not get a service pension, this is the single biggest financial difference between the two tracks.
